numerical_failure.observed_behavior: With Numba JIT on Python 3.14.3, multiplying a complex infinity by a real float returns a NaN imaginary part: nb_mul(complex(inf, 1.0), 2.0) gives (inf+nanj). Multiplying the real by the complex, nb_mul(2.0, z), also gives (inf+nanj). Real is promoted to complex(x, 0j) and the full complex kernel is used.
numerical_failure.expected_behavior: Match CPython 3.14 pure-Python results: mul(z, 2.0) and mul(2.0, z) both give (inf+2j) for z=complex(float('inf'), 1.0).
trigger_conditions: Python 3.14 or later (numba gates the fix on utils.PYVERSION >= (3, 14))
complex operand with an infinite component multiplied by a real float
mixed real/complex arithmetic, where numba promotes the real to complex(x, 0j) and uses the full complex kernel
jit-compiled function, e.g. jit(mul) with def mul(z, x): return z * x

input_output_examples.input: z = complex(float('inf'), 1.0); mul(z, 2.0) with mul(z, x): return z * x, jitted with numba

numerical_characteristics.magnitude: large finite value 1e200 used so multiplication can overflow before recovery; signed zeros and infinities also involved
category_specific_evidence: Python 3.14 added NaN recovery for complex multiplication and division so that infinities computed as nan+nanj are recovered (numba/cpython/numbers.py diff adds PYVERSION >= (3,14) branch when real and imag are both NaN).
Recovery logic: if an operand is infinite, its components are set to copysign(1.0 or 0.0) and NaN components of the other operand are replaced by copysign(0.0, ...) before recalculation.
Test TestComplexNaNRecovery builds special values from -0.0, +0.0, 1, -1, 1e200, -inf, +inf, nan products and runs mul and div.
Issue #10780: mixed real/complex arithmetic (e.g. complex(inf,1.0)*2.0 gives inf+nanj in numba but inf+2j in CPython 3.14); signed zeros matter for mixed + and - such as 2 - 0j.

PR discussion: CPython complex division depends on FMA; math.fma(-areal, ratio, aimag) gives -4.816661538840688e-217 versus 0.0 for plain arithmetic on M1 mac for z=(1e200-1j), w=(1e200-1j); not reproduced on linux-aarch64.

PR discussion: complex division NaN sign-bit difference; numba returns NaN with payload 0xfff8000000000010 while CPython returns 0x7ff8000000000000 for z=(-inf + NaN payload) / w=(-0.0 -inf j); commenter believes CPython fails to propagate payload.
reproduction_risks: Results depend on Python version (3.14+ only) and on whether FMA is used by the platform, so the division result differs across M1 mac and linux-aarch64.
NaN sign and payload bits may differ from CPython; comparisons must account for payload and sign rather than only value.
Mixed real/complex operations take a different code path in CPython 3.14 than in Numba (issue #10780), so results can diverge even when complex kernels agree.
